purpose: Advanced failure-mode diagnostics beyond binary correct/wrong finished-state plates. Each mode maps symptom → cause → action for high-risk knots.

mode_types.label: Construction failure
mode_types.description: Structure never formed correctly while tying.

mode_types.label: Seating failure
mode_types.description: Looks tied but does not lock under the first real load.

mode_types.label: Material failure
mode_types.description: Right knot geometry, wrong line behavior or diameter mismatch.

mode_types.label: Load-path failure
mode_types.description: Load concentrates on one leg, coil, or side.

mode_types.label: Service failure
mode_types.description: Started good; degraded after guides, abrasion, or heat cycles.

mode_types.label: Misapplication
mode_types.description: Correctly tied knot used for the wrong connection job.

modes.symptom: Braid coils look alternating-open or uneven before locks.
modes.cause: Inconsistent tension or reverse weave direction mid-series.
modes.action: Retie with even tension; count and maintain direction.

modes.symptom: Weave slides on the leader before half-hitches engage.
modes.cause: Too few wraps, slick braid, or insufficient pre-tension.
modes.action: Add wraps for material; seat weave firmly before locks.

modes.symptom: Leader shows whitening, kink, or deep deformation under the weave.
modes.cause: Diameter mismatch or over-cinching a soft leader.
modes.action: Match diameters; wet and draw progressively; retie if crushed.

modes.symptom: After a day of casting, the junction hangs in guides.
modes.cause: Bulky locks or frayed braid shoulder at the transition.
modes.action: Trim tags, re-dress locks, or switch to a slimmer connection family.

modes.symptom: Doubled strands cross before cinching.
modes.cause: Loop twisted while forming the overhand.
modes.action: Retie keeping doubled strands parallel.

modes.symptom: Final loop catches on hook point, split ring, or lure body.
modes.cause: Hardware not fully passed or seated around the eye only.
modes.action: Open, re-pass hardware cleanly through the big loop, reseat.

modes.symptom: One strand looks tighter than the other after seating.
modes.cause: Standing and tag not pulled evenly.
modes.action: Wet and draw both legs evenly; retie if already deformed.

modes.symptom: Knot creeps on slick braid or fused superline.
modes.cause: Wrong terminal choice for the material.
modes.action: Use verified braid-friendly terminal (e.g. Uni with more wraps, NanoFil variant).

modes.symptom: Twist column shows gaps or loose sections.
modes.cause: Insufficient tension during the initial twists.
modes.action: Retie under continuous tension; keep legs even.

modes.symptom: Reverse wraps stack or jump instead of progressing.
modes.cause: Loss of tension while transitioning to reverse wraps.
modes.action: Maintain tension; re-wrap reverse series cleanly.

modes.symptom: One loop leg bears visibly more load.
modes.cause: Asymmetric finishing or uneven initial legs.
modes.action: Equalize legs before final locks; retie if already set wrong.

modes.symptom: Used as a terminal to a lure eye.
modes.cause: Double-line loop job confused with terminal eye job.
modes.action: Use Bimini for double-line/system building; pick a terminal knot for the eye.

modes.symptom: One wrap column collapses or overlaps.
modes.cause: Uneven wrap counts or diameter mismatch.
modes.action: Balance wraps; consider a different join for large diameter steps.

modes.symptom: Both tags exit the same direction.
modes.cause: Incorrect center exit during final draw.
modes.action: Retie ensuring opposite tag exits.

modes.symptom: Thinner line buries under thicker coils.
modes.cause: Too large diameter step for a blood knot.
modes.action: Use a join designed for mismatch (Alberto/FG family) or taper leaders.

modes.symptom: Junction frays after repeated guide passes.
modes.cause: Slight shoulder or tag stub abrasion.
modes.action: Trim flush; inspect often; switch family if bulk remains.

modes.symptom: Return wraps cross randomly over outbound wraps.
modes.cause: Lost wrap order on the return series.
modes.action: Retie keeping outbound and return ordered.

modes.symptom: Tag exits the wrong side of the leader opening.
modes.cause: Final pass direction error.
modes.action: Retie with correct exit path.

modes.symptom: Finished barrel can be pushed or telescoped after seating.
modes.cause: Insufficient seating tension or too few wraps.
modes.action: Seat firmly wet; add wraps if material is slick.

modes.symptom: Junction hangs in smaller guides.
modes.cause: Bulky barrel relative to guide ID.
modes.action: Dress tags; consider FG or slimmer join for that rod.

modes.symptom: Loop size shrinks under a firm pull test.
modes.cause: Incorrect return path through the overhand or insufficient wraps.
modes.action: Retie holding loop size while seating; verify return path.

modes.symptom: Wraps bunch or reverse during final draw.
modes.cause: Dry cinch or uneven wrap spacing.
modes.action: Wet, keep wraps ordered, draw steadily.

modes.symptom: Stiff fluoro kinks or refuses to seat cleanly.
modes.cause: Material too stiff for the loop variant in hand.
modes.action: Use a fluoro-appropriate loop variant or different terminal strategy.

modes.symptom: Loop used on a lure that needs a snug eye seat.
modes.cause: Loop applied where a tight terminal is safer (cover, trebles, etc.).
modes.action: Switch to Palomar/Uni/Clinch family for pinned terminals.

modes.symptom: One barrel remains open while the other is tight.
modes.cause: Uneven wrap quality or incomplete seating.
modes.action: Retie the weak side; ensure both barrels form fully.

modes.symptom: Barrels pass through each other instead of meeting.
modes.cause: Insufficient standing-line pull or crossed tags.
modes.action: Pull standing lines so barrels slide together and meet.

modes.symptom: Braid side creeps under load.
modes.cause: Too few wraps on slick braid.
modes.action: Increase braid-side wraps; retest.

modes.symptom: Connection hangs after repeated casts.
modes.cause: Double barrels too bulky for guide train.
modes.action: Trim tags flush; consider FG/Alberto for guide-heavy work.

modes.symptom: Main-line wraps reverse mid-series.
modes.cause: Lost wrap order while under tension.
modes.action: Retie with consistent wrap direction.

modes.symptom: Leader loop is twisted through the barrel.
modes.cause: Leader doubled section rotated during wraps.
modes.action: Keep leader loop flat; retie.

modes.symptom: Junction can be pushed open after seating.
modes.cause: Under-tensioned final draw.
modes.action: Wet and seat firmly; add wraps if needed.

modes.symptom: Heavy leader will not grip fine braid cleanly.
modes.cause: Extreme diameter mismatch.
modes.action: Step leaders or use a connection verified for that mismatch.

modes.symptom: Wraps look uneven or reverse direction mid-coil.
modes.cause: Lost count or line spun while wrapping.
modes.action: Retie counting wraps; keep wraps stacked side-by-side.

modes.symptom: Coil sits above the eye with a visible gap.
modes.cause: Not fully drawn after wetting.
modes.action: Wet, draw hard, and seat the coil flush to the eye.

modes.symptom: Wraps cross over each other instead of spiral cleanly.
modes.cause: Tag pulled across standing line mid-build.
modes.action: Retie keeping wraps ordered and parallel.

modes.symptom: After fishing, the tag has worked back out of the coil.
modes.cause: Short tag or soft line creep under load cycles.
modes.action: Leave a longer tag and recheck after first fish.

modes.symptom: Uni barrel stays open or elongated.
modes.cause: Too few wraps or uneven tension.
modes.action: Add wraps for the material and draw both sides evenly.

modes.symptom: Barrel does not slide fully to the eye under load.
modes.cause: Dry line or insufficient pull test.
modes.action: Wet and pull-test until barrel seats against the eye.

modes.symptom: Tag did not pass back through the loop correctly.
modes.cause: Mis-threaded final pass.
modes.action: Retie; the tag must exit the loop after wraps.

modes.symptom: Barrel slides under moderate load on slick line.
modes.cause: Wrong knot for fused/slick mono.
modes.action: Use a verified slick-line terminal or more wraps.

modes.symptom: Doubled strands cross before the overhand.
modes.cause: Twisted loop while passing the eye.
modes.action: Keep strands parallel; retie if crossed.

modes.symptom: Overhand loop traps lure hardware incorrectly.
modes.cause: Passed the wrong part of the doubled loop.
modes.action: Retie sending only the free loop over the hardware.

modes.symptom: Knot sits crooked at the eye after the first pull.
modes.cause: Uneven draw on the standing line.
modes.action: Draw both legs evenly while seating.

modes.symptom: Tag frays at the seat after a few casts.
modes.cause: Sharp eye edge or short tag.
modes.action: Inspect the eye, leave a safer tag, retie if abraded.

modes.symptom: Shank wraps overlap instead of lying side-by-side.
modes.cause: Lost wrap spacing while building.
modes.action: Retie with even side-by-side wraps.

modes.symptom: Line exits the eye in the wrong orientation.
modes.cause: Started from the wrong side of the eye.
modes.action: Retie matching the intended eye exit.

modes.symptom: Coil climbs toward the eye under load.
modes.cause: Not seated down the shank.
modes.action: Draw so the coil stays on the shank.

modes.symptom: Hook twists relative to the line after fish.
modes.cause: Uneven wrap tension.
modes.action: Retie and pull-test for hook alignment.

modes.symptom: Shank wraps overlap instead of lying side-by-side.
modes.cause: Lost wrap spacing while building.
modes.action: Retie with even side-by-side wraps.

modes.symptom: Line exits the eye in the wrong orientation.
modes.cause: Started from the wrong side of the eye.
modes.action: Retie matching the intended eye exit.

modes.symptom: Coil climbs toward the eye under load.
modes.cause: Not seated down the shank.
modes.action: Draw so the coil stays on the shank.

modes.symptom: Hook twists relative to the line after fish.
modes.cause: Uneven wrap tension.
modes.action: Retie and pull-test for hook alignment.

modes.symptom: Only barrel wraps present—no true haywire twists.
modes.cause: Skipped the mutual-twist section.
modes.action: Retie with true twists before barrel wraps.

modes.symptom: Cut tag leaves a sharp wire point.
modes.cause: Tag not finished safely.
modes.action: Barrel-wrap the tag and finish without a spear.

modes.symptom: Twists are open and do not lock.
modes.cause: Insufficient twist count or tension.
modes.action: Add true twists under even tension.

modes.symptom: Wire work-hardens and snaps at the twist.
modes.cause: Repeated bend cycles at the same spot.
modes.action: Retie fresh wire; do not rework a fatigued twist.

modes.symptom: Leader exits off-center from the fly-line core.
modes.cause: Needle path not centered.
modes.action: Retie with a centered insertion path.

modes.symptom: Fly-line coating splits at the insertion.
modes.cause: Oversized needle or dry force.
modes.action: Use a compatible needle size; inspect coating.

modes.symptom: Leader pulls free under moderate load.
modes.cause: Too shallow an insertion or no finish wraps.
modes.action: Increase insert depth and finish correctly.

modes.symptom: Water entry softens the joint after a day.
modes.cause: Unsealed coating breach.
modes.action: Retie; consider a sealed finish method.

modes.symptom: Wrap column looks short or sparse for the line.
modes.cause: Under-counted wraps for the material.
modes.action: Retie with the profile wrap count for that material.

modes.symptom: Leader exits at a sharp angle from the wraps.
modes.cause: Not drawn in-line while seating.
modes.action: Seat wraps so the exit continues the line of pull.

modes.symptom: Heavy braid digs into light leader under wraps.
modes.cause: Diameter gap too large for this family.
modes.action: Step diameters or use a different join family.

modes.symptom: Wraps loosen after hard runs.
modes.cause: Insufficient seat or wet-draw.
modes.action: Re-seat under progressive load; retie if wraps open.

modes.symptom: Wrap column looks short or sparse for the line.
modes.cause: Under-counted wraps for the material.
modes.action: Retie with the profile wrap count for that material.

modes.symptom: Leader exits at a sharp angle from the wraps.
modes.cause: Not drawn in-line while seating.
modes.action: Seat wraps so the exit continues the line of pull.

modes.symptom: Heavy braid digs into light leader under wraps.
modes.cause: Diameter gap too large for this family.
modes.action: Step diameters or use a different join family.

modes.symptom: Wraps loosen after hard runs.
modes.cause: Insufficient seat or wet-draw.
modes.action: Re-seat under progressive load; retie if wraps open.

modes.symptom: Doubled strands cross before the overhand.
modes.cause: Twisted loop while passing the eye.
modes.action: Keep strands parallel; retie if crossed.

modes.symptom: Overhand loop traps lure hardware incorrectly.
modes.cause: Passed the wrong part of the doubled loop.
modes.action: Retie sending only the free loop over the hardware.

modes.symptom: Knot sits crooked at the eye after the first pull.
modes.cause: Uneven draw on the standing line.
modes.action: Draw both legs evenly while seating.

modes.symptom: Tag frays at the seat after a few casts.
modes.cause: Sharp eye edge or short tag.
modes.action: Inspect the eye, leave a safer tag, retie if abraded.

modes.symptom: Loop size shrinks under the first real load.
modes.cause: Overhand or return path incorrect.
modes.action: Hold loop size while seating; verify return path.

modes.symptom: Wraps bunch instead of lying ordered.
modes.cause: Lost tension while wrapping.
modes.action: Retie keeping wraps side-by-side.

modes.symptom: Loop fails or creeps on fluoro/slick mono.
modes.cause: Knot family misapplied to the material.
modes.action: Use a verified loop for that material.

modes.symptom: Tag works free after repeated casts.
modes.cause: Short tag or soft mono creep.
modes.action: Leave a safer tag and recheck mid-session.

modes.symptom: Connection formed as a girth hitch instead of square interlock.
modes.cause: One loop pulled through the other incorrectly.
modes.action: Retie as a true loop-to-loop interlock.

modes.symptom: Loops enter twisted relative to each other.
modes.cause: Rotated while connecting.
modes.action: Open, re-seat squarely, or reconnect.

modes.symptom: One loop is far smaller and cuts the other.
modes.cause: Loop size mismatch under load.
modes.action: Match practical loop sizes.

modes.symptom: Loop legs abrade at the contact point.
modes.cause: High cycle load on mono loops.
modes.action: Inspect mid-session; retie nicked loops.

modes.symptom: Barrel coils stay open on the host.
modes.cause: Too few wraps or soft tension.
modes.action: Add wraps and seat firmly against the host.

modes.symptom: Leader exits with a snag shoulder.
modes.cause: Not drawn in-line with the host.
modes.action: Seat so the exit continues the host line of pull.

modes.symptom: Host coating splits or softens under the barrel.
modes.cause: Over-cinch or incompatible host.
modes.action: Retie with progressive tension; inspect host.

modes.symptom: Barrel creeps on the host after load cycles.
modes.cause: Insufficient seat for the material.
modes.action: Re-seat or retie; verify host diameter fit.

modes.symptom: Loop size shrinks under the first real load.
modes.cause: Overhand or return path incorrect.
modes.action: Hold loop size while seating; verify return path.

modes.symptom: Wraps bunch instead of lying ordered.
modes.cause: Lost tension while wrapping.
modes.action: Retie keeping wraps side-by-side.

modes.symptom: Loop fails or creeps on fluoro/slick mono.
modes.cause: Knot family misapplied to the material.
modes.action: Use a verified loop for that material.

modes.symptom: Tag works free after repeated casts.
modes.cause: Short tag or soft mono creep.
modes.action: Leave a safer tag and recheck mid-session.

modes.symptom: One side twists more than the other.
modes.cause: Uneven hand tension while twisting.
modes.action: Retie with matched twist counts.

modes.symptom: Braid used where mono-main is required.
modes.cause: System misapplication.
modes.action: Use the verified material pairing for this knot.

modes.symptom: Finished junction shows a sharp cutting angle.
modes.cause: Not drawn square.
modes.action: Seat so the join is compact and square.

modes.symptom: Outer strands abrade after guide contact.
modes.cause: Bulky twist on small guides.
modes.action: Dress tags; consider a slimmer join.

modes.symptom: Twist column shows gaps or stacked reverse wraps.
modes.cause: Lost twist count or reverse direction mid-build.
modes.action: Retie with continuous even twists.

modes.symptom: One loop leg carries more load than the other.
modes.cause: Legs not equalized before locking.
modes.action: Equalize legs, then finish locks.

modes.symptom: Locking wraps are too few for the line.
modes.cause: Rushed finish on braid.
modes.action: Add the practical wrap count for the material.

modes.symptom: Loop legs fray at the twist shoulder.
modes.cause: Abrasion or repeated high load.
modes.action: Retie; inspect for nicks before reuse.

modes.symptom: Only one overhand pass completed.
modes.cause: Stopped early on a double-pass knot.
modes.action: Complete both passes before the final draw.

modes.symptom: Join stays open and asymmetric after pulling.
modes.cause: Dry mono or uneven draw.
modes.action: Wet and pull both standing lines evenly.

modes.symptom: Join fails on a large diameter step.
modes.cause: Surgeon family overstressed by mismatch.
modes.action: Use a diameter-tolerant join instead.

modes.symptom: Tags chafe the standing line after fishing.
modes.cause: Tags left long and free.
modes.action: Trim tags and recheck after first fish.
